title: Restriction preserves vanishing of ideal-power products
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $K$ a quasi-coherent ideal sheaf [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-ideal-zero-set-affine], $F$ a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent], $V$ an open subset of $X$, and $n\geq 0$. Form $K^nF$ as the image of multiplication, with $K^0=\mathcal O_X$ and identity inclusion [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-module-product-stalk]. Write $K|_V$ for the comap ideal and $F|_V$ for restriction [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits]. Then $(K^nF)|_V=0$ if and only if $(K|_V)^n(F|_V)=0$, where zero means a zero object in the category of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category].

source.place: Tag 01YD, lemma-prepare-filter-support, proof: restriction of I^n F to X minus Z'; with Schemes Tag 01I8 and Modules Tag 01CD. Read online at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01YD.

proof.text: The recursively defined sheaf power inclusion is monic by two-step induction. On every affine open its range equals the corresponding ideal power, by the affine-power clause; the module realization of Mathlib IdealSheafData power has the same ranges. The existing affine-range subobject helper therefore gives equality of the two subobjects and an isomorphism commuting with their inclusions.

An isomorphism of ideal modules commuting with their inclusions induces an isomorphism of their products with any module: after whiskering, the multiplication maps have equal image subobjects. Apply this to the power identification on X and on the open.

Apply the existing single-product restriction clause to the ideal-sheaf-data power and F. Restriction preserves monomorphisms because sections on an open immersion are sections on the image open. The equal image subobjects yield an isomorphism of the product objects.

For an open immersion, comap commutes with ideal powers by the affine ideal formula and Ideal.map_pow. Combine the two product isomorphisms, restriction of the first, the single-product comparison, and this equality; IsZero is invariant under isomorphism.

lean.statement:
theorem idealPowerProduct_restrict_isZero_iff {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (K : X.IdealSheafData) (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent]
    (V : X.Opens) (n : ℕ) :
    IsZero ((restrictFunctor V.ι).obj
      (idealModuleProduct (idealSheafPower K.toModulesι n).2 F)) ↔
    IsZero (idealModuleProduct (idealSheafPower (K.comap V.ι).toModulesι n).2
      ((restrictFunctor V.ι).obj F))
